name: Shape K - Vocabulary Development (Retrieval-Focused)
description: Vocabulary lesson built on the research consensus: words are presented explicitly in context, then met repeatedly through spaced retrieval practice and varied input before generative productive use.
pedagogical_justification:
Research on L2 vocabulary instruction converges on four principles that this shape operationalises.

(1) Selection: teach high-frequency, useful words (Nation, 2017; Nation & Waring, 1997). Words chosen should be learnable as a word family (stem + inflected/derived forms) so that affix knowledge multiplies the repetitions available (Bauer & Nation, 1993).

(2) Explicit first meeting in context: an efficient initial encounter (brief meaning, form, pronunciation, phonemic script) gives learners something to retrieve later. Isolated word lists are inferior; words should be presented in a meaning-rich context and connected to known words or cognates (Alizadeh, 2016; Nation, 2017; Nisbet & Tindall, 2015).

(3) Retrieval and spacing: retrieval (recalling a form or meaning rather than re-reading it) strengthens the form-meaning link, and spaced repetition beats massed repetition for long-term retention (Kim & Webb, 2022 meta-analysis, 98 effect sizes; Nation, 2017). In-class retrieval activities (word cards, gap-fill, matching) set up the learner to meet the word again.

(4) Varied meetings and generative use: meeting a word in new contexts and using it productively deepens processing. Deeper task-induced involvement (need, search, evaluation) predicts stronger learning (Laufer & Hulstijn, 2001; Kim, 2011). A productive stage that forces use of the target words converts receptive knowledge into productive knowledge (Nation, 2017).

The shape therefore moves: Lead-in (context) → Explicit presentation (M/F/P in context) → Controlled retrieval practice → Varied input meeting (reading/listening where the words recur) → Generative use (freer productive task) → Recycling (spaced retrieval of the words for a later lesson). Stage times assume a 46-minute lesson.
main_aim_format: By the end of the lesson, learners will be better able to use [target vocabulary] to [function] in the context of [topic].

example_lesson_plan.header:
Objective:
By the end of the lesson, learners will be better able to use a set of film vocabulary items (blockbuster, cast, plot, scene, soundtrack, special effects, trailer, screenplay) to describe and discuss films they have seen.
Teacher:
Ed Rush
Date:
[DD-MM-YY]
Duration:
46 minutes
CEFR Level:
B1
Lesson Shape:
K (Vocabulary Development)
Materials:
Student Book page 122, slideshow, audio track, vocabulary word cards
Assessment:
Retrieval game scores, generative task observation
Systems:
Vocabulary

stages.stage_aim: To activate schema and set the film context
stages.procedure:
- Display three film stills (sci-fi, action, drama) on PP. In pairs, Ss name the genre and say one thing they know about each type of film. 2 min. Feedback.
- Ask: What makes a film good? Elicit ideas (story, actors, music, explosions). Write ideas on the board.

stages.stage_aim: To present target vocabulary clearly in context
stages.procedure:
- Display the 8 target words in a table: word + phonemic script + context sentence. E.g. blockbuster /ˈblɒkbʌstə/: 'That new superhero film was a huge blockbuster.'
- Model pronunciation. Drill chorally and individually.
- Elicit/check meaning with concept-checking questions (What does a 'cast' include? Is a 'scene' long or short?).
- Draw attention to form: 'screen' + 'play' = screenplay. Which of these are compound words? 1 min.

stages.stage_aim: To retrieve form and meaning under controlled conditions
stages.procedure:
- Activity 1 (receptive retrieval): Ss match word cards to definitions on their desks. Self-check against answers on PP. 2 min.
- Activity 2 (productive retrieval): Ss close books. Display L1 translations or pictures one at a time; Ss say the English word and write it on mini whiteboards. Reveal spelling after each. 3 min.
- Language feedback on spelling and pronunciation.

stages.stage_aim: To meet the target words again in new contexts while listening
stages.procedure:
- Ss open books to page 122. Explain they will listen to a short film review containing the target words in new contexts.
- Play the audio once. Ss tick the words they hear. 3 min. Pair check.
- Play again. Ss answer two gist questions (Is the review positive? What type of film is it?). 3 min. Feedback.

stages.stage_aim: To use the target vocabulary productively in a freer task
stages.procedure:
- In pairs, Ss choose a film they both know. They must use at least 5 of the target words to describe it (plot, cast, soundtrack, special effects...). 4 min.
- Pairs join into groups of four and compare. Each pair reports one film using the words. 4 min.
- Content feedback first, then language feedback on target word use.

stages.stage_aim: To consolidate and set up spaced retrieval for the next lesson
stages.procedure:
- Quick-fire retrieval round: teacher says a definition, Ss say the word. 8 items, 2 min.
- Tell Ss the same words will reappear in next lesson's warm-up (spaced retrieval).
- Exit question: Which word was most useful for you? Why? 1 min.
